entries.title: See who owns what in a workspace, choose List, Grid or Cards, and open folders instantly
entries.summary: A workspace's list now shows each item's owner with their photo or initial, and the people whose items are in each folder. Choose List, Grid or Cards; Markdrop remembers it. Folders open at once, even on slow connections.
entries.body:
- **Owners on every row.** Members see who owns each document, page and file, and **You** on their own. Folders show the people whose items are inside, and when something in them last changed.
- **List, Grid or Cards.** List is the default: name, kind, owner, updated, who can open it and **⋯**. Grid and Cards are tidier tiles with less text. Your choice is remembered on this device, everywhere in the workspace.
- **Folders open instantly.** Clicking a folder in the list, the sidebar or the breadcrumb switches right away, and items you pointed at are often already loaded. Pages no longer preload every link in the sidebar, so slow connections stay free for what you click.
- **Folder actions on the row.** Admins can rename, move, set what new items start as, or delete a folder from its row's **⋯** menu.
- **AI apps.** `list_workspace_items` says who owns each item, and `list_folders` says when each folder last changed and whose items are in it.

entries.title: Page exports look like the page, and a page stays a page
entries.summary: Exported HTML and PDFs no longer draw a page's title over its cover, exports always download or print where you are, and a page can no longer get stuck as a Markdown document.
entries.body:
- **Exports look like the page.** In the HTML file and the PDF, the cover runs across the top, the icon sits on the cover's bottom edge and the title is below them, never on the cover.
- **Exports stay where you are.** The file downloads in the tab you're in (or the print dialog opens there for a PDF), and if Markdrop refuses an export, the dialog says why. An AI app's export link that has expired opens a short page saying so, instead of an error.
- **A page stays a page.** **Open in the classic editor** is gone from a page's menus. **Edit as Markdown** shows the page's source only for now, with **Edit with blocks** on screen to go back; a reload always opens blocks again.
- **Switch back to the page editor.** A page that was switched to the classic editor shows its owner and editors a banner and a **More actions** item to make it a page again, on markdrop.in and on your workspace's own domain.

entries.title: Edit pages on your workspace's own domain, and Request edit access
entries.summary: Anyone who may edit a page can now edit it right on the workspace's own domain, like docs.acme.com, instead of going back to markdrop.in. Readers who can't edit a page can ask for edit access from its ⋯ menu.
entries.body:
- **Edit on your domain.** Signed in on the workspace's domain, a member, someone the page is shared with as **Can edit**, the owner or anyone with the edit link opens the page straight into the editor: text and title, images, sub-pages, page properties, AI writing tools and **Version history**, with **Saving…/Saved** and who's on the page.
- **Share with people on the domain.** Anyone who may share the page can see who has access, add people as **Can view** or **Can edit** (with **Notify people**), remove them and copy the link, right on the domain.
- Who can open it in general, its password and expiry, its link, deleting it, and workspace settings stay on markdrop.in, so a domain can never make a private page public: the owner's **⋯** menu opens the same page there (**General access on markdrop.in ↗**, **Change link on markdrop.in ↗**, **Delete on markdrop.in ↗**).
- The sign-in on your domain still works only there and only for that workspace's pages, and every page still runs its normal access check.
- **Request edit access.** Someone who can read a page but not edit it asks from the page's **⋯** menu, with an optional note, on markdrop.in or on the domain. The page's owner gets an email with **Approve** and **Decline** (the workspace's admins, when the page has no owner who can be reached) and an entry under **Access requests**. Approving lets them edit that page only; they get an email either way.

entries.title: AI in pages: rewrite, draft, summarize, translate, and ask a page questions
entries.summary: Pages have AI built in. Editors rewrite a selection, draft with /ai, turn notes into a page, find action items, summarize, translate a whole page and get alt text. Signed-in readers can ask a page questions.
entries.body:
- **Ask AI** on a selection (or **⌘ J**): improve, shorten, fix spelling and grammar, change tone, translate, turn into a checklist or a table, explain. Every result is a suggestion you accept or discard.
- **/ai** on an empty line drafts in the page's own blocks, with the page in mind. **New page › Start from notes** turns pasted notes into a structured page.
- In the page's **⋯** menu: **Summarize page** (a Summary note at the top), **Find action items** (to-dos with person and date chips), **Suggest title & icon** and **Translate…**, which makes a translated copy next to the page and leaves the original as it is.
- Images you upload get suggested alt text.
- **✦ Ask** for signed-in readers: questions about the page, answered from it and from the embedded items you can open, with links to the sections they use. It works on a workspace's own domain too.
- No AI for visitors who aren't signed in or for encrypted documents. Admins can turn **AI features** off for a workspace.
- Only the text a request needs goes to Anthropic, and Markdrop keeps usage counts, never the text. Fair use during the beta: 30 requests a minute and 300 a day per person.
- The same writing tools in the Markdrop Guides editor, and three new MCP tools: `translate_page`, `summarize_page` and `suggest_page_meta`. See [AI in pages](/pages/ai).

entries.title: Pages: version history, with changes highlighted and one-click restore
entries.summary: Every page keeps its earlier versions. Open Version history from the page's ⋯ menu to see each one as the page looked then, what changed against the page now, and restore any of them. A restore is itself a version, so it can be undone.
entries.body:
- **Saved for you:** one version per 10 minutes of editing and one when you leave the page, plus a version before and after every change an AI app makes, labelled with the app's name.
- **Version history** opens over the page: versions grouped by day, who saved each one, and the one that matches the page now. **↑** and **↓** step through them; on a phone, tap one to open it.
- **Show changes** highlights what's only in that version (green) and what's only in the page now (red, struck through).
- **Restore this version** asks first, then saves the restore as a new version, keeping the page as it was. It waits if someone else is editing the page.
- Every version is kept for 30 days, then the last one of each day for a year. Only people who can edit a page see its history. End-to-end encrypted documents have none.
- Images nothing in a page or its history shows any more are deleted after 30 days.
- New MCP tools: `list_page_versions`, `get_page_version` and `restore_page_version`.

entries.title: Export pages as Markdown, HTML or PDF
entries.summary: Download a page as portable Markdown, one self-contained HTML file or a PDF, with its images and the sub-pages you can open. Items a reader can't open are exported as "Locked item", never by name.
entries.body:
- **⋯ › Export…** on any page: pick **Markdown**, **HTML** or **PDF**.
- **Markdown** any app reads: callouts become labelled quotes, columns follow one another, people and dates become text, embedded files become links. With images, a `.zip` with an `images` folder.
- **HTML:** one file in the page's look, images inside, that opens anywhere, even offline.
- **PDF:** your browser's print dialog with the page laid out for paper: light, no menus, the cover on top, no blocks split across sheets.
- **Include sub-pages:** a folder for each one you can open, linked to each other; the PDF prints them after the page.
- **Readers can export** unless the page's editors switch that off in its ⋯ menu.
- An end-to-end encrypted document's browser saves its Markdown with **Download Markdown**.
- AI apps export with the new `export_page` MCP tool.

entries.title: Workspace templates: use any page as a template
entries.summary: Use a page as a template for your workspace or just for you, with its sub-pages and images. It shows up in New page and Add a sub-page, a folder can start every new page from one, and {{title}}, {{date}}, {{author}} and {{folder}} are filled in.
entries.body:
- **⋯ › Use as template** on any page: choose **Everyone in** your workspace or **Just me**, a name, a description and an emoji, and whether to include the sub-pages you can open. Images are copied with it.
- **New page** and **Add a sub-page** show your workspace's templates first, then yours, then the built-in ones, each with a preview.
- **A folder's default template:** admins choose what New page in a folder starts from, like a PRD template in `product-hub/02-prds`. Anyone can still pick Blank or another template.
- **Placeholders:** `{{title}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{author}}` and `{{folder}}` become the page's title, the day, the person making it and its folder.
- **Manage templates:** rename, edit (a template is a page, in the same editor), delete, and drag to reorder. Admins manage the workspace's templates; members can rename or delete the ones they saved. Editing a template never changes pages already made from it.
- Templates never show up in lists, search, the sidebar, folder pages or AI apps' document search. Viewers and people outside the workspace never see them.
- AI apps: `list_page_templates` (optionally for one `workspace`) lists them with ids, `create_page` takes a template's id or slug, `set_page_properties` with `template` turns a page into a template and back, and the new `save_page_as_template` and `set_folder_default_template` save one and set a folder's default.

entries.title: AI apps add image files and covers to pages, no base64
entries.summary: Your AI app can now add an image file from disk to a page, up to 20 MB, and make it the page's cover or icon. The file goes straight to storage with one curl command, instead of being pasted into the chat as base64.
entries.body:
- **`create_page_image_upload`** returns a storage address and the exact `curl` command that sends the file there; **`complete_page_image_upload`** checks the size, the SHA-256 and that the file really is a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image, then returns `asset:<id>` and the Markdown `![alt](asset:<id>)` to put in the page.
- **Covers and icons:** pass that `asset:<id>` to `set_page_properties` as `cover` or `icon`. Like every page image, it shows only to people who can read the page.
- **`copy_page_asset`** copies an image from one page to another you can edit, as a new image of that page.
- Images up to 20 MB this way; an upload not finished within 6 hours is discarded. `upload_page_image` still takes small images as base64, up to 10 MB.

entries.title: Pages: choose a page's link, and change it without breaking the old one
entries.summary: Change a page's link from its ⋯ menu, with the whole new address shown as you type. The old link keeps working on markdrop.in and on your workspace's own domain, and AI apps can set a page's link when they create it.
entries.body:
- **Change link…** in a page's **⋯** menu (owners): type the new slug, see it checked as you type and the full address it will have, with your domain, folders and parent pages.
- **The old link redirects.** On markdrop.in and on your workspace's domain, sub-page addresses included. Change it again and every earlier link goes to the newest one. Embeds and mentions of the old link keep working, with nothing to rewrite.
- **MCP:** `create_page` takes `slug`, the new `set_slug` tool changes the link of a page, document or file, and `publish_document` takes `editor: "blocks"` to publish a page. A taken link is an error that names it, never a silent rename.
- **API:** `POST /api/v1/pages` takes `slug`, and `GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/slug-check?new_slug=` says whether a link is free and what the full address would be.

entries.title: AI apps can duplicate pages, list a workspace's members and mention people by name
entries.summary: Three additions for teams that build pages with an AI app: duplicate_page copies a page with its images, list_workspace_members gives the ids to mention people, and a mention written with just a name finds the member it means.
entries.body:
- **duplicate_page** copies a page you can read, with its properties and its own copies of its images, into a folder or page you choose, or next to the original. The copy is yours, and a locked page gives an unlocked copy, so a locked template can be the start of a new page. Sub-pages come along when you ask.
- **list_workspace_members** lists the members of a workspace you're in: name, account id and role, and email addresses for admins.
- In a page, `:person[Ada Lovelace]` without an id now finds the one member of the page's workspace with that name when the page is saved. A name that matches nobody, or more than one member, stays plain text, and the AI app is told which.

entries.title: Trash: everything you delete can be restored for 30 days
entries.summary: Deleting a document, page, file or folder moves it to Trash for 30 days instead of deleting it at once. Undo right after, or restore it from Trash, and it comes back exactly where it was.
entries.body:
- **Moved to Trash · Undo** right after every delete.
- **Trash** in the sidebar lists what you deleted: what it is and its link, where it was, who deleted it, when, and the days left. **Restore** puts it back with the same link, folder, parent page, access and people; **Delete forever** removes it for good.
- Deleting a **folder** moves it and everything inside to Trash; restoring brings the whole folder back. Workspace admins see and restore everything deleted from their workspace.
- The delete dialog now names exactly what goes: "Delete the page “Product Docs Playbook” (/EegpMKD)?", with how many sub-pages go with it. Lists show each item's kind next to its link, so two items with the same title are easy to tell apart.
- A deleted item's link stays reserved, and shows **This page is in the trash** (with **Restore**) to people who could edit it; everyone else gets the usual 404. Its files aren't served to anyone while it's in Trash.
- AI apps: `delete_document` moves to Trash and returns `restore_until`; new `restore_document` and `list_trash`; `permanent: true` deletes forever (owners, and admins for their workspace's Trash).

entries.title: Mentions that notify: a bell, emails and Notify people
entries.summary: Mention someone on a page and they're told: a notification under the new bell at the top of Markdrop, and an email, both opening the page at the block that mentions them. Only people who can open the page are notified.
entries.body:
- **The bell:** an unread badge, the list newest first with who, what, the page and when, **All** / **Unread** and **Mark all read**. Choosing one opens the page at the block and highlights it. A bottom sheet on phones.
- **Who's told:** each person newly mentioned (or named on a sign-off block) who can open the page. Never you, never someone already mentioned before your change, never someone who can't open the page, and a page they lose access to later shows without its title.
- **Email:** at most one per page every 10 minutes, with the mentions batched. Turn it off in **Settings › Account** (**Email me when someone mentions me**) or from the email's own link; the bell keeps working.
- **Share › Notify people** (was **Email them**): the email with your message, plus a notification for people with an account.
- **MCP:** pages an AI app writes notify the same way, and three new tools: `list_notifications`, `mark_notifications_read` and `share_with_people`. See [Mentions and notifications](/pages/mentions-and-notifications).

entries.title: Pages: sign-off blocks, approved by one named person and locked once signed
entries.summary: Add a Sign-off block to a page, name who signs it and give it options such as Approved for production or Not approved. Only that person can choose; Markdrop records the decision with their name and the time, and nobody can change the block, or the section above it, until they clear it.
entries.body:
- **/ › Sign-off** in any page in a workspace: choose who signs, the label and up to six options, and whether signing locks the section above.
- **Only the person named can sign**, not the owner, not an admin, not an AI app acting for someone else. The decision is stored by Markdrop, never in the page's Markdown, so it can't be faked by editing.
- **Once signed**, the block (and with *lock above*, everything from the previous heading down to it) can't be changed or deleted, in the editor, in Markdown, from VS Code or through MCP. The signer can change or clear their decision; a workspace admin can remove a signed block, and that's recorded.
- Sign-offs show on the block, as pills under the page's title and in **Version history** ("Signed off by Riya: Approved for production").
- Two new MCP tools: `list_signoffs` and `sign_off`. See [Sign-off](/pages/sign-off).

entries.title: Page properties, and folders as tables and boards
entries.summary: Give a folder's pages typed properties such as Status, Owner and Target date. They show under each page's title, and the folder opens as a table or a board: drag a card to change its status.
entries.body:
- **Properties under the title:** Select and Multi-select with coloured options, Person (a workspace member, with their picture), Date with a calendar, Text, Link (an address or a page), Number and Checkbox. Anyone who can edit the page changes them in place; readers see the ones that are set.
- **A folder is the database:** add a property once and every page in the folder has it. Members and admins add, rename and remove properties. Removing one never deletes a page's value.
- **Table and board views** in the folder: a sticky header, resizable columns, filter, sort and group, and cells you edit in place. On the board, drag a card between columns to change its value. Members save up to 20 views per folder.
- **Only what you can open:** views list just the pages you can read, and a linked page's title shows only to people who can open it.
- **For AI apps:** `set_folder_properties` and `list_folder_pages` are new, `set_page_properties` and `create_page` take `properties`, and `get_page` returns them. See [Properties and views](/pages/properties-and-views).

entries.title: Automatic covers for pages, and 32 new covers
entries.summary: A new page gets a cover picked for what it's about, from 44 calm covers now. Remove it in one click and it never comes back; workspace admins can turn Auto covers off.
entries.body:
- New pages get one of Markdrop's covers by themselves: AI reads the title and the first lines and picks one, or the page's words are matched when AI is off. It fades in a moment after the page opens. An untitled, empty page gets its cover once you've named it and started writing.
- 32 new covers, for roadmaps, meetings, releases, research, design, runbooks, people, finance, marketing, legal, support, data, security, docs and more, in a new **Shapes** group. **Pick for me** in the cover picker chooses one for the page.
- An automatic cover says **Auto** when you hover it. **Remove** is one click, and a removed cover is never added back. A duplicate keeps its original's cover; templates and encrypted pages never get one.
- **Auto covers** on the workspace settings' **Advanced** tab, next to **AI features**, turns it off for a workspace.
- Pages made before this got a cover the same way, once.
- MCP: `create_page` picks a cover (`auto_cover`, default true) and says which in `cover`; `set_page_properties` with `cover: "auto"` picks one again. See [Automatic covers](/pages/overview#automatic-covers).

entries.title: Pages: write with blocks, embed your files, nest pages inside pages
entries.summary: A page is a Markdrop document you write with blocks, like in Notion: colours, columns, templates, sub-pages, a cover and an icon, and your PDFs, videos, images and HTML pages embedded live. Each reader sees an embedded file only if they can open it.
entries.body:
- **New page** in a workspace or folder, **Create** › **Page**, or **Open in block editor** on a document you already have. Pick a template: release notes, a customer how-to, a QA test plan, a product spec, meeting notes, a runbook, or blank.
- **Always editable.** If you can edit a page, it opens ready to type: no Edit or Done. It saves as you type, holds the page for you from your first key or click, and lets go when you leave or after three idle minutes. Everyone else sees the same page, read only, and who's editing.
- Type `/` for a menu grouped by kind, with a preview of each block: headings, to-dos, toggles and toggle headings, callouts with an emoji and colour, tables, code, math, Mermaid diagrams, a table of contents, bookmarks, YouTube, Loom and Figma embeds, dates and people. Markdown shortcuts and Notion's keyboard shortcuts work as you type.
- **Colours and layout:** text and background colours, underline, coloured blocks, **columns** (drag a block beside another), **nesting** with Tab, and buttons that add blocks when clicked.
- **Blocks:** select several to move, colour, duplicate or delete them together, drag them with a drop line, and copy a link to any block. Resize and align images, set table column widths and header rows, colour cells, and caption code.
- **Paste** from Google Docs, Notion, Word, web pages and GitHub, keeping headings, lists, tables, links and formatting.
- **Covers:** twelve covers in four styles, or your own image, repositioned by dragging.
- **Embed** and **mention** your Markdrop files and documents. A reader who can't open one sees a locked placeholder without its title.
- **Sub-pages** follow their parent's access until you set their own, and show in breadcrumbs, the page tree and your workspace's sidebar.
- Paste or drop images: they belong to the page and only its readers see them.
- Pages keep a copy in your browser until the server has it.
- A page is still Markdown underneath, so VS Code and AI apps read and write it. New MCP tools create pages, add blocks while you're editing, and embed files.

entries.title: No more "Sign in to read" on your workspace's domain when you're already signed in
entries.summary: Members signed in on markdrop.in could still get the sign-in screen on their workspace's own domain, usually after the 12-hour sign-in there ran out. Those pages now open on their own.
entries.body:
- When the sign-in on a workspace's domain has run out (it lasts 12 hours), Markdrop renews it in the background the next time you open a page that needs it, instead of showing **Sign in to read** followed by the workspace's name.
- This also works on a page you opened earlier in the same tab. Before, Markdrop checked only once per tab.
- Pages that need sign-in show **Opening…** while Markdrop checks, instead of showing the sign-in screen for a moment first. This applies on markdrop.in too.
- A sign-in that has run out is no longer reported as **You don't have access**.

entries.title: See who's viewing a document or file, live
entries.summary: Documents and files now show who's reading them right now, with the section each person is on. People with access appear by name; everyone else appears as an anonymous animal. Your AI app can ask too.
entries.body:
- **Who's viewing** in the header of every document and file: avatars, and a list of everyone here with the section, page or video moment they're on.
- **Names only for people with access:** the owner, workspace members and people you invited. Everyone else, signed in or not, is "Anonymous Otter" and friends.
- **Show me as anonymous**, for viewers who'd rather not be named. **Show who's viewing** in Share turns it off for a document.
- **Encrypted documents** show only how many people are reading.
- **AI apps:** the MCP server's new `get_viewers` and `set_presence` tools (28 tools now).
- Shown live and never stored. See [See who's viewing](/sharing/see-whos-viewing).

entries.title: Connect AI tools to any guide's MCP server in one click
entries.summary: Every published guide has its own MCP server. Its pages now have Connect to AI: readers add the guide to Cursor or VS Code in one click, or connect Claude, Claude Code or ChatGPT with the steps shown.
entries.body:
- **Connect to AI** in every page's **Copy page** menu (behind **More** on a phone): copy the MCP server URL, **Add to Cursor**, **Add to VS Code**, or the steps for Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT and other MCP apps.
- **Your guide's MCP server** in Settings › Ask AI: its URL (your own domain when you have one), install buttons, and **Test it**, which lists the tools the live server offers.
- **Your choice:** admins can hide Connect to AI on pages. It's on by default.
- **Public pages only:** private pages and sections never reach the server, and guides that ask readers to sign in don't offer it.
- The **Publish** screen shows the server's URL once the guide is live.
highlights: Add to Cursor and VS Code in one click

entries.title: Export a guide and run it on your own server
entries.summary: Download any guide as a folder of Markdown and files, and serve it yourself with the open-source engine and one Docker command. No lock-in.
entries.body:
- **Settings › Export & self-host** downloads the guide as a zip: every page as Markdown, the sidebar, theme (your custom theme included), brand, redirects, changelog, API reference and the images and files the pages use. Export the live guide or the drafts. Guides admins only.
- **Private pages and sections** are left out by default, or exported as public pages if you choose: a self-hosted guide has no reader sign-in.
- **One command serves it:** `docker run -p 8080:8080 -v "$PWD/my-guide:/site:ro" ghcr.io/himanshkukreja/markdrop-guides`. The image is built for amd64 and arm64 and published with each release. It rebuilds when a file changes and keeps the last good build if one fails.
- **What stays with Markdrop:** the editor, reviews, Ask AI, Insights and the Fix list, private-page sign-in and GitHub sync. The export turns them off in the folder, so nothing half-works.
highlights: Export the live guide or the drafts

entries.title: The Guides studio has its own address: guides.markdrop.in
entries.summary: Markdrop Guides, where you write and publish your guides, now opens at guides.markdrop.in. markdrop.in/guides is the page about Markdrop Guides, for everyone.
entries.body:
- **guides.markdrop.in** is the studio: your guides, the editor, Insights, the Fix list and every guide's settings.
- **No second sign-in:** signed in on markdrop.in, you're signed in on guides.markdrop.in too. Signed out, Markdrop asks you to sign in once and brings you back.
- **markdrop.in/guides** is the page about Markdrop Guides for everyone. Signed in, its button says **Open your guides**.
- **Old links keep working:** a markdrop.in/guides/… address (an email, a bookmark) opens the same screen on guides.markdrop.in.
- **Signing out** of Markdrop Guides asks whether to sign out of Markdrop too; signing out on markdrop.in signs you out of both.

entries.title: Markdrop Guides: import from GitHub and keep in sync
entries.summary: Bring a repository's docs into a guide (Markdown, GitBook Git Sync, Mintlify, Docusaurus or MkDocs) and keep it in sync: every push to the branch updates the guide.
entries.body:
- **Import from GitHub** is a new way to start a guide. Pick a repository, a branch and a folder; Markdrop Guides works out the format and previews the pages and sidebar before anything is imported.
- **Five formats:** a plain Markdown folder, GitBook Git Sync (`SUMMARY.md`), Mintlify (`docs.json` or `mint.json`, tabs included), Docusaurus (`sidebars.js`, read without running it) and MkDocs (`mkdocs.yml`). Their callouts, tabs, steps, cards and expandable sections become the guide's own blocks, and images and PDFs become the guide's files.
- **Keep in sync:** with the Markdrop Guides GitHub app installed, every push updates the guide's drafts, or publishes it automatically if you choose. A renamed file keeps its page and history, and its old address redirects.
- **GitHub is the source of truth** for the pages it brought: the editor shows where a page comes from, with **Edit on GitHub**. Pages you add in the editor are never touched.
- **Private or public:** the app reads only the repositories you choose, read-only. A public repository imports without it.
- **Settings › GitHub** has the sync history, **Sync now**, the mode, and **Disconnect** (the pages stay). An OpenAPI file found in the repository can become the guide's API reference.
highlights: Mintlify, Docusaurus, MkDocs, GitBook and plain Markdown
Read-only GitHub app: Contents and Metadata only

entries.title: Markdrop Guides: the Fix list, what to fix next
entries.summary: One ranked list of what to fix next in a guide: where readers leave a page, searches that find nothing, questions Ask AI couldn't answer, video and PDF drop-off, broken links and pages AI agents can't use, each with an AI-drafted fix to review in the editor.
entries.body:
- **Ranked by impact:** the readers each problem affects, how serious it is and how recent. Nothing is flagged on a handful of visits; each item says how sure it is, and pages still collecting show under **Needs more readers**.
- **Evidence for every item:** how far readers got down the page section by section, a video's viewers over time, the wordings readers searched for or asked, their comments.
- **Draft a fix:** a rewritten section, an answer to add, a new page outline or a corrected link, shown as a change. **Open in editor** offers it as a suggestion over the section; nothing is published until you publish, and the next publish marks it fixed.
- **Start, Mark fixed, Dismiss** with a reason. A fixed item whose problem comes back reopens.
- **AI agents counted apart from readers:** reads by ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and others, Markdown and llms.txt reads, MCP calls, and what agents search for and don't find.
- **Private like Insights:** no cookies, nothing that identifies a reader, nothing sent when a browser asks not to be tracked. A **Fix list** tab with its open count, and **N to fix** on the Guides home cards.

entries.title: Markdrop Guides: private pages and sections, free
entries.summary: Keep a guide public and make some pages, groups or sections private: for your team, a customer's people by email or @domain, or partners with a password. On every guide, with no plan to upgrade.
entries.body:
- **Who can open this page** in the editor's Page tab: inherit, public, the team, specific people or email domains, or a password. A rule for a whole sidebar group in Settings.
- **Private sections** inside a public page: type `/` and choose **Private section**. Everyone else sees a lock card with the way in.
- **Readers sign in with their email:** a one-time link, no Markdrop account needed. Team members use Sign in with Markdrop; partners type the password.
- **Access requests** from the lock page reach the guide's admins by email; approving adds the reader to the rule. **Access history** lists every change.
- **Preview as** a public reader, a team member, an email address or someone with a password, and warnings for public pages that link to private ones.
- **Nothing private leaks:** private pages and sections are left out of search, llms.txt, the sitemap, the MCP server, feeds and Ask AI for readers who can't open them, and every publish checks it.

entries.title: Markdrop Guides: reset a guide's design
entries.summary: Put a guide's design back to the one it started with, after its GitBook import or when it was created, with a list of what changes first and Undo after.
entries.body:
- **Reset design** at the bottom of Design goes back to the design the guide had right after its import, or the one it was created with.
- **The dialog lists what changes** (theme, brand colours, logo, fonts, colour mode, corners, custom theme, custom CSS) before anything happens.
- **Saved like Save design:** readers see it after you publish, and Undo puts back the design you had.
- **Kept:** your saved design templates and uploaded logos. Pages, navigation, domains and other settings don't change.
- In Design, the button that drops unsaved edits is now called **Discard changes**.

entries.title: Markdrop Guides: embed files that render
entries.summary: Put an interactive HTML demo, a zipped site, a PDF or a video from Markdrop in a guide page as a live block that updates when you replace the file.
entries.body:
- **Markdrop file** block in the editor (`/markdrop`): pick from your files or the guide's workspace, paste a link, or upload.
- **Interactive HTML and zipped sites** run in the page in a locked sandbox on Markdrop's file domain; **PDFs** get page controls and zoom; **videos** play in the docs player with captions and chapters.
- **Replace the file on Markdrop** and every guide shows the new one, no republish. Pin a version to keep one.
- **Only files anyone with the link can open** show to readers; anything else is a notice that names nothing.
- **Text version** for search, Ask AI, llms.txt and screen readers: your summary, a PDF's text, a video's transcript.
- **Insights › Embedded files**: views, use, where viewers stop a video, the PDF page readers reach.

entries.title: Markdrop Guides: a changelog for your guide
entries.summary: Write what shipped as changelog entries in Markdrop Guides: your guide gets a changelog page, a page per release, RSS and JSON feeds, and entries in search and Ask AI.
entries.body:
- **Changelog** is a new section of every guide, next to Pages. Write an entry with a title, a one-line summary and details in the same editor as your pages, and pick its date, kind (New, Improved or Fixed) and area.
- **Products and versions:** name the products you ship and say which one an entry changed and the version it needs. Readers filter by product and see only what's new since their version.
- **Media and links:** an image or a video from the guide's files, highlights, a Try it button and the pages the change touched.
- **Coming next:** list what you're working on above the releases.
- **Readers get** `/changelog` with a Changelog tab, a page per entry, RSS, JSON Feed and Markdown feeds, a link preview per entry, and entries in the guide's search and Ask AI, all in the guide's own theme.
- **Entries publish with the guide:** new, edited and removed entries show on Publish and in What changed, and go through reviews when a guide requires them.
- **Already have release notes?** A page called Changelog, Release notes or What's new with a dated heading per release turns into entries in one click, including after a GitBook import.
highlights: A preview in your guide's saved design before you publish
RSS and JSON feeds on your guide's own address

entries.title: Encrypted documents: an optional password, recovery and a look under the hood
entries.summary: Require a password on top of the link, get back into a document with a pasted link or a saved key, save copies in your browser, and see exactly how a document is protected.
entries.body:
- **Also require a password:** readers need the link and the password. It's checked in their browser and never sent to Markdrop. After publishing, **Copy link** and **Copy password** are separate, so you can send them separately.
- **A stronger format:** AES-256-GCM with keys derived by HKDF-SHA256, a key commitment checked before decrypting (so a wrong or old key is told apart from altered content), and padding so the stored size doesn't give away the exact length. Older documents keep opening, and saving one upgrades it without changing the link.
- **Recovery:** paste the full link on the no-key screen, keep the key through signing in, and fall back to a key saved in this browser when the link's key doesn't open the current version.
- **Readers choose** whether a device remembers the key, and signing out offers to forget saved keys.
- **No lost edits:** a save over a newer version, or after the owner issued a new key, is refused instead of written over it.
- **Save a copy** of an encrypted document in your browser, encrypted with a new key or unencrypted.
- **How this is protected:** a panel showing the format, the algorithms, where the key came from and the start of what our servers store.
- **Images from other sites** in an encrypted document wait for the reader's click, and PostHog and Google Analytics don't run on an encrypted document's page.

entries.title: Markdrop Guides (beta): build and host guides for your product
entries.summary: Write help centers, product guides, API references and handbooks in the browser, pick a theme, and publish a fast guide with search and Ask AI. Free while it's in beta.
entries.body:
- **Create a guide** in a workspace or on your own, blank or from a template (product guide, API reference, help center), at a free `<name>.guides.markdrop.in` address.
- **Import from GitBook:** pages, images, navigation, icons, brand and old links come across, with a report of what needs a look before you publish.
- **A visual editor** with a slash menu for callouts, steps, tabs, cards, code and images with dark versions, or plain Markdown. Drafts save as you type, every save is a version, and one person edits a page at a time.
- **Six themes** (Clean, Editorial, Technical, Minimal, Playful, Help center), your logo and colours with checked contrast, fonts, corners, colour mode and custom CSS.
- **Publish** when you're ready: see what changed, follow the build, and put an earlier publish back in seconds. Turn on reviews to have changes approved first.
- **Guides roles** (Admin, Reviewer, Editor, Viewer), separate from workspace roles, with per-guide roles and a history of changes.
- **For readers:** search, Ask AI with sources, light and dark, and a Markdown copy of every page, `llms.txt` and an MCP server for AI tools.
- Coming soon: your own domain, password-protected and members-only guides, and GitHub sync.

entries.title: CLI 0.5.1: install fix, Windows on Arm, sends listed under your account
entries.summary: The one-line installer no longer prints an error, Windows on Arm gets a working build, and send and the local MCP server use the token saved by markdrop login.
entries.body:
- The install script for macOS and Linux started with stray characters, so `curl … | sh` printed a "not found" error before installing. It now runs cleanly.
- On Windows on Arm, the PowerShell installer installs the x64 build, which runs under emulation, instead of failing.
- `markdrop send` and the local MCP server now use the token saved by `markdrop login` when `MARKDROP_TOKEN` isn't set, so your shares appear in your account. `send` also takes `--token`.
- `markdrop mcp --help` lists all eleven tools, and `markdrop upload` on a folder explains how to publish a website or send the folder instead.

entries.title: Restore old file versions, transfer a workspace, and leave what's shared with you
entries.summary: A file's Settings lists its versions to restore or delete, workspace owners can hand over ownership, and people added to a document or file can remove themselves.
entries.body:
- **Versions:** a file's **Settings** lists its last five versions. Restore one to make it current again at the same link, or delete an old one to free space.
- **Transfer ownership:** a workspace owner can make another member the owner from the **People** tab, and becomes an admin.
- **Remove me:** people added to a document or file can take themselves off it from **Shared with me** or the item's menu.
- **New edit secret:** the owner of a document can replace a leaked edit secret from **Document settings**.
- **Fixes:** the keyboard-shortcuts setting now turns off F and /, admin-only workspace controls say "Admins only" consistently, and zipped sites no longer count skipped files towards their limits.

entries.title: Send API requests from the docs, and see each feature
entries.summary: Try it on every API page now calls the live API, and the guides have screenshots in light and dark, short clips and narrated videos.
entries.body:
- **Try it sends the request.** Fill in the form on an endpoint page and choose **Send request** to call the live API from your browser. You see the status, the time it took, the headers and the body. Requests that create, change or delete something ask you to confirm first, and a document published from Try it expires after a day.
- **Screenshots, clips and videos** across the guides, from publishing and sharing to workspaces, analytics, Send and the AI pages. Screenshots follow your light or dark theme; click one to enlarge it.
- **A new changelog.** Search, filter by product, and see what changed since the CLI version you have.
highlights: Try it calls the live API

entries.title: Workspace header, account menu and title fixes
entries.summary: Pages on a workspace's own domain show its logo and name together, account menus open over the document bar, and a document that starts with its own title no longer shows it twice.
entries.body:
- On a workspace's own domain, the top bar shows the workspace logo next to its name, lined up with the rest of the page. A wide logo that already contains the name is shown on its own.
- The account menu in the top bar opened behind the document's toolbar. It now opens on top, on markdrop.in and on workspace domains.
- A document whose Markdown starts with its own main heading shows only that heading, even when it differs from the document's title. The title still names the page in the top bar, the browser tab and link previews.
- Publishing a password-protected document while signed in could leave the page loading forever. It now opens the Published panel with your links.
- Parts of a document's page that load when you first use them, like the share dialog, no longer flash the full-page loader.

entries.title: Docs with Ask AI
entries.summary: docs.markdrop.in: every guide, an API reference, and an assistant that answers from the docs with links to the exact section.
entries.body:
Markdrop now has documentation at **docs.markdrop.in**.

- **Ask AI** answers from these docs, cites the exact section for each point, and highlights it when you open the source.
- **API reference** for every public endpoint, with curl, JavaScript, Python and CLI examples and a Try it form that builds the command for you.
- **For your AI app:** every page has a Markdown version, the whole site is in `/llms.txt`, and a docs MCP server lets Claude, Cursor or VS Code search the docs as you work.
- **Copy page** and **Open in Claude or ChatGPT** on every page, and a mark on sections that changed since your last visit.
highlights: Answers link to the exact section

entries.title: Creator analytics
entries.summary: See how each document, PDF, video and audio file you publish is read or watched, live and over time.
entries.body:
Every document and file you own now has its own analytics page, and **Analytics** in your dashboard shows them all together.

- **Video and audio:** how many people are still watching at 0:30, 25%, 50%, 75% and the end, where most of them leave, and how playback went.
- **Markdown documents:** how many read to the end, how far readers get section by section, and what they copy and which links they click.
- **PDFs:** how many readers reach each page.
- **Live now:** who is reading or watching right now.

Your own views are never counted, and you can download a document's numbers as CSV. AI apps connected to Markdrop can ask for the same numbers with the new `get_document_analytics` tool.

entries.title: Light is the default theme
entries.summary: Markdrop now opens in the light theme unless you choose dark or system.
entries.body: New visitors see Markdrop in the light theme. Your choice is remembered per browser: pick dark, or system to follow your device, from the theme switch.

entries.title: Simpler workspaces
entries.summary: One sidebar for your files and workspaces, folders you can drop files onto, and sharing in one dialog.
entries.body:
Workspaces were redesigned around one drive-style sidebar: **My files**, **Shared with me**, **Recent** and each workspace's folder tree.

- **Folder view** shows who can open what in a folder at a glance, and you can drop files onto it to upload them.
- **Preview as** shows a workspace the way someone else would see it.
- **One share dialog** with three presets: *Only people added*, *{Workspace} team* and *Anyone with the link*. Passwords and expiry are under **More options**, for documents too.
- **Request access:** people who can't open a document can ask for access, and you decide from an email or the app.
- **Search** with :kbd[⌘K] across your documents, files and folders.

Documents and files now open in a new tab, at the address **Copy link** gives you, on your workspace's own domain when it has one.

entries.title: Passwords and expiry from the share dialog
entries.summary: Set or remove a document's password and expiry from the share dialog, including a new one-hour expiry.
entries.body:
The share dialog's **More options** now sets a password and an expiry for Markdown documents as well as files, including **On a date…**, and the new one-hour option. The dialog also shows the document's real address.

For scripts, `PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/settings` changes the password and expiry without resending the content.

A document published without a title now takes one from its first heading or first line.

entries.title: Workspaces, folders and custom domains, rebuilt
entries.summary: Share whole folders, keep one access level per document at every address, and run your workspace on your own domain more safely.
entries.body:
Workspaces, folders and custom domains were rebuilt on one access rule: a document has one access level at every address it has, on markdrop.in and on your workspace's domain alike.

- **Share a folder** with a single link. People see only the items they can already open.
- **Renamed addresses** send readers to the new one, and old addresses are never handed to someone else.
- **Custom domains** are re-checked every day. A domain whose DNS no longer points at Markdrop stops serving after three days of failed checks.
- **Editors and workspace members** can replace a file from the viewer.
- **AI apps** can list workspaces and folders, file documents, create folders and move items, and the CLI can upload straight into a folder.

Existing workspace links keep working.

entries.title: CLI 0.5.0: publish into workspaces
entries.summary: Upload straight into a workspace folder, choose the address, and list your workspaces from the terminal.
entries.body:
```bash
markdrop workspaces                     # your workspaces, roles and live domains
markdrop workspaces Acme                # its folders
markdrop upload spec.pdf --workspace Acme --folder guides/setup
markdrop upload demo.mp4 --slug q3-demo
```

- `--workspace` takes a workspace's id, name or custom domain; `--folder` an existing folder path.
- The printed link is on the workspace's custom domain when it has a live one.
- `--slug` picks the address and fails before uploading if it is taken.
- `markdrop mcp` gains `list_workspaces` and `list_folders`, and its `upload_file` takes `workspace`, `folder` and `slug`.

On the hosted MCP server, seven workspace tools arrived at the same time: `list_workspaces`, `list_folders`, `list_workspace_items`, `add_to_workspace`, `remove_from_workspace`, `create_folder` and `move_to_folder`.

entries.title: Replace a file and keep its link
entries.summary: Swap the video, PDF or page behind a link you already shared, keep the last five versions, and publish videos up to 2 GB.
entries.body:
Re-recorded the demo? Revised the PDF? Replace the file and everyone with the link gets the new one. The link, its access, title and view count stay the same.

- **Versions:** the last five versions of each file are kept, and you can restore any of them. A restore is itself a new version, so nothing is lost.
- **Bigger files:** video and audio up to 2 GB each, sent in parts and checked by SHA-256 before they go live. Storage is 20 GB per account, earlier versions included.
- **Audio files** (MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG) get their own player, and videos show a poster frame before they play.
- **From anywhere:** replace a file on markdrop.in, with `markdrop replace`, or from an AI app.
highlights: Video and audio up to 2 GB

entries.title: CLI 0.4.0: upload, replace and versions
entries.summary: Publish files from the terminal and swap them behind the same link, with resumable uploads and JSON output for scripts.
entries.body:
New commands: `upload`, `replace`, `versions`, `restore`, `info`, `login` and `logout`.

- Uploads are hashed, sent four parts at a time, verified by Markdrop, and resume when you run the same command again.
- `--json` prints one JSON object and nothing else, for scripts and CI.
- `markdrop login` saves an API token so you don't need `MARKDROP_TOKEN` in every shell.
- `markdrop mcp` gains `upload_file`, `replace_file`, `list_file_versions`, `restore_file_version` and `get_file_info`, so an AI app on your computer can publish files from disk.

entries.title: Replacing a video over 25 MB works again
entries.summary: Replacing a video file used the 25 MB limit for documents and refused larger videos.
entries.body: Replacing the file behind a video link now uses the video size limit, and checks your storage with the old file counted as freed.

entries.title: Send files from an AI app on your computer
entries.summary: markdrop mcp, a local MCP server in the CLI, lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code share and receive files peer to peer.
entries.body:
Add `markdrop mcp` to an AI app on your computer and ask it to "share these three PDFs" or "download this share link into ~/Projects".

- `share_files`, `share_status`, `stop_share` and `receive_share` run on your machine; files go straight to the recipient.
- Well-known secret locations such as `~/.ssh` and `.env` files are refused.
- `markdrop send` and `get` now use a relay when a direct connection between networks isn't possible.
- On the hosted server, `list_shares` and `get_share_status` show your shares and check a share link.

entries.title: Connect Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps
entries.summary: Markdrop's MCP server lets your AI assistant publish, read and update your documents, after you approve it on Markdrop.
entries.body:
Paste `https://api.markdrop.in/mcp` into Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or another MCP app, sign in to Markdrop and approve. There's no key to copy.

- Ask for "a Markdrop doc of these notes" and get a link that renders.
- Publish HTML pages, read and update documents, change who can open them, and see how they're read.
- Two permissions, *Read your documents* and *Publish and change documents*, approved per app.
- Disconnect any app from **Settings → Connected apps**.

Assistants can't read end-to-end encrypted documents or get past a password.

entries.title: Peer-to-peer shares survive a dropped connection
entries.summary: A sender whose connection drops takes their link back, recipients wait for them, and transfers between different networks go through a relay.
entries.body:
- A sender whose browser reconnects takes its share link back instead of being locked out of it.
- Recipients who open the link while the sender is away wait up to 10 minutes for them to return.
- When the two computers can't connect directly, the transfer goes through a relay. The relay can't read the encrypted connection.

entries.title: Large HTML files publish from VS Code
entries.summary: HTML and other text files up to 25 MB now publish and sync from VS Code; larger self-contained pages used to fail.
entries.body: Self-contained HTML pages with inlined images or fonts between 10 and 25 MB failed to publish from VS Code. The limit for files synced from the editor is now 25 MB, the same as for uploads.

entries.title: Privacy page and privacy choices
entries.summary: A privacy page explains what Markdrop collects, and visitors from the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland choose whether to allow analytics.
entries.body:
- The new [privacy page](https://markdrop.in/privacy) explains what Markdrop collects and why.
- Visitors from the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland are asked before product analytics run. Declining, or sending Global Privacy Control, keeps analytics from storing anything in your browser.
- **Privacy choices** in the footer reopens the choice at any time.
- Product analytics never see your documents' addresses or what you type.

entries.title: A new Markdrop
entries.summary: Every screen was redesigned on one design system, with a new reader, a new upload page and a light theme.
entries.body:
- A new reader for documents and files, full screen or framed, with clearer messages when a link needs a password or a sign-in.
- A new upload page, editor and publish settings.
- Settings pages for your account, API tokens and workspaces.
- A light theme alongside dark.

entries.title: Send many files to many people from one link
entries.summary: One share link now serves up to 10 recipients at once, carries several files, and shows who is downloading.
entries.body:
- Add several files to one share and send them all with one link.
- Up to 10 people can download from the link at the same time.
- See who is connected and how far along each download is.
- Recipients are told when the sender closes the link.
- Links made in the browser work with `markdrop get`.

entries.title: Share documents with people
entries.summary: Choose who can open a document when you publish it, and add people by email as viewers or editors.
entries.body:
- Pick who can open a document when you create it, and change it later from the document.
- Add people by email with **Can view** or **Can edit**. They sign in to open it.
- Folders in a workspace are part of the address, so a document's link shows where it is filed.

entries.title: Workspaces on your own domain
entries.summary: Create a workspace, invite your team, and serve its documents on your own domain with your branding.
entries.body:
- Workspaces with members and roles, and invitations people accept.
- Serve a workspace's documents on a domain you own, verified through DNS.
- Your logo and accent colour on your domain, and link previews in your brand.
- Video files with their own player.

entries.title: End-to-end encrypted documents
entries.summary: Encrypt a document in your browser so Markdrop stores only ciphertext and the key lives in the link.
entries.body:
Turn on encryption when you publish and the document is encrypted in your browser with AES-256-GCM before it is sent. The key is part of the link after `#k=`, which browsers never send to a server, so Markdrop can't read the document.

Anyone with the full link can read it; anyone without the key part can't, including Markdrop and AI apps.
